 JUDGMENT

The petitioners have filed this claim petition U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act, 1989, against the respondents for seeking compensation on account of death of one Sri.Ajith @ Ajith Kumar S/o Sriram, in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

02. The brief facts of the case of the petitioners is as under:
That on 04.12.2018 at about 11.50 p.m, the deceased Ajith @ Ajith Kumar was proceeding in the Omni Car bearing No.KA-03-MJ-2959 along with other friends and the same was driven by its driver from Bengaluru to Devanahalli, when they reached near (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.3910/2019 Kanmangala Palya Gate, BB Road,
Devanahalli Taluk, at that time a Innova Car bearing No.KA-03-NB-9119 which belongs to respondent No.1, driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner, at very high speed, without giving any signal came from Bengaluru to Devanahalli and dashed to the Car from behind.

Due to which the deceased sustained grievous injuries and immediately after the accident he was shifted to Government hospital,
Devanahalli and after first aid, he was shifted to Shusrusha hospital and then shifted to Prolife hospital, Hebbala and admitted as inpatient for 120 days and finally on Sriram vs Suhalya Travels Pvt Ltd on 14 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113974092/

sentences.text: 3 02.04.2019 the doctor declared that he was dead.

The petitioners have spent more than Rs.20,00,000/- towards medical expenses, food and nourishment charges,
funeral and last rites.
Prior to the accident the deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 22 years and was doing private business as own work and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m and was the only bread winner in his family.
Due to death of the deceased, the petitioners are put to great mental shock, irreparable loss and mental agony.

The accident is occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending Innova Car and in this regard the BIAL Traffic Police have registered a case (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.3910/2019 against driver of the offending car in Crime No.173/2018 for the offences punishable U/Sec 279, 304(A) of IPC.
The respondent No.1 is the RC Owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the said offending vehicle,
are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- to the petitioners together with interest at the rate of 18% p.a with costs.
03. On service of notice, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared before the tribunal through their counsels, but only the respondent No.2 has filed objections.
Later the counsel for the petitioners have filed application to implead respondents No.3 to 8 as they are all Charge sheeted accused.
Later notice was issued to respondents No.3 to 8.
The respondents No.3 to 5 did not appeared and hence they were placed exparte.

The respondents No.6 to 8 have are appeared before the tribunal,
but not filed their objections.

04. The respondent No.2 in its objections has denied the entire case of the petitioners and further denied age, income, occupation of deceased and manner of accident, involvement of the vehicle,
expenses incurred by the petitioners, dependency of the petitioners with the deceased and contended that the driver of the offending car was not holding valid (SCCH-3) 7 M.V.C.No.3910/2019 and effective driving licence at the time of accident as on the date of accident,
the owner of the car has contravened the provisions of M.V. Act and Rules and they committed the breach of terms and conditions of the policy and admits that this respondent has issued policy of insurance in favour of respondent No.2 in respect of Car bearing No.KA-03-NB-9119 and the liability of this respondent if any, is limited to terms and conditions of the policy.

The car in question did not involved in the accident nor caused accidental injuries to the petitioner and on the date of accident the car was being driven in a reasonable speed and careful manner and there was no rashness or negligence on the part of the driver of car and the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the omni car, in which deceased persons and petitioner were travelling.
The petition is bad for non-joinder of proper and necessary parties.

The compensation claimed is highly excessive, exaggerated and hence, pray for dismiss the petition with costs against respondent No.2.
05.

Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following issues have been framed by my learned predecessor: -

sentences.text: 01. Whether petitioners prove that they are the LRs/dependents of deceased Sri.Ajith @ Ajith Kumar?

02. Whether petitioners prove that deceased Sri.Ajith @ Ajith Kumar was died in RTA arising out of the accident alleged to have been taken place on 04.12.2018 at about 11.50 p.m, near Kannamangala Palya Gate, BB Road, Devanahalli Taluk, Bengaluru District, due to negligent act of driver of Car bearing registration No.KA-03-NB-9119 as alleged in the petition?
03.
Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
04 . What order or award?
06. In order to prove their case, the petitioner No.1 was got examined as PW.1 and got marked 22 documents as Ex.P.1 to 22 and closed their side evidence.
07. By way of rebuttal, the respondent No.2 did not lead evidence inspite of sufficient opportunity has been given.
Hence, the respondent No.1 evidence is taken as nil and closed its side evidence.

08. Heard both sides.
09.

My findings on the aforesaid Issues are as under:-
 (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.3910/2019  Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.4 : As per final order  for the following:-
 REASONS 10. Issues No.1:- Petitioner No.1 filed affidavit stated that, he is the father, petitioner No.2 is the mother and petitioner No.3 is the sister of the deceased.

To prove the said Issue No.1, he has produced notarized copies of Aadhaar cards of deceased and other petitioners as per Ex.P.19 to 22 which shows that the petitioners are the father, mother and sister.
There is no dispute in his cross- examination regarding relationship of the petitioners with the deceased.
So on perusal of these documents, it is true that the petitioners No.1 to 3 are the legal representatives and dependents on the deceased.
Accordingly, this Issue is answered in the affirmative.
11. Issues No.2:-
The petitioner No.1 got himself examined as PW.1 and he has given evidence in the form of the affidavit and he has reiterated the petition averments therein.

Though, he has been Sriram vs Suhalya Travels Pvt Ltd on 14 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113974092/
5 (SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.3910/2019 elaborately cross-examined by the respondent No.2 counsel, but nothing is brought on record to disbelieve the case of the petitioners that due to rash and negligent driving of the offending car by its driver, deceased sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident and later died during the course of treatment.

sentences.text: On perusal of the documents, Ex.P.1 is the FIR registered at BIAL Traffic Police against driver of the offending Car.
Ex.P.2 is the Complaint which shows that due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending car, the accident took place and deceased sustained injuries.
12. The accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending Car.

Ex.P.3 and 4 are Spot Mahazar and Spot Sketch showing the place of accident near Kannamangala Palya Gate, BB Road and the Innova Car came from right side to left side and dashed against the Omni Car in which deceased was proceeding, which is not disputed.
Ex.P.5 is copy of Notice U/Sec.133 of IMV Act issued to the owner of the offending Car.

Ex.P.6 is copy of Reply to notice which discloses that the owner of the offending Car has stated that one Madhusudhan.V was driving the car and he had a (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.3910/2019 valid driving licence as on the date of accident.
Ex. P.7 is copy of IMV report which shows involvement of both vehicles in the accident.
Ex.P.8 is the Wound certificate which shows that the deceased sustained five injuries and all are grievous in nature.
Ex.P.9 is Death intimation issued by Prolife hospital.
Ex.P.10 is Inquest report of deceased Ajith @ Ajith Kumar.
Ex.P.11 is Post mortem report of deceased Ajith @ Ajith Kumar shows the cause of death is due to septicemia as a result of multiple injuries sustained.
Ex . P.12
is the important document of Investigation Officer.
After completion of the investigation filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending Car for the offences punishable U/Sec 279, 337, 338, 304(A) of IPC and Sec.198(a) of IMV Act.
Ex.P.13 is Death summary.
Ex.P.17 is Lab report and Ex.P.18 is CT scan report.
These documents clearly goes to show that the deceased sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending car.
Accordingly, Issue No.2 is answered in the affirmative.

13. Issue No.3:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the (SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.3910/2019 death of the deceased Ajith @ Ajith Kumar, who died in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

The PW.1/petitioner No.1 has stated that prior to accident deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 22 years and was doing private business as own work and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m. Due to untimely death of the deceased, the petitioners are put to great financial loss, loss of love and affection and mental agony.
14.
It is the duty of the petitioners to prove age of the deceased as on the date of accident.
The petitioners have not produced any birth certificate, school records or SSLC marks card of the deceased to show the exact date of birth of the deceased.
However, they have produced Ex.P.19 Aadhaar card of deceased.

Eventhough the said document is not authenticated document for the proof of age of any person, but in the absence of other evidence, said document can be relied upon and according to which his birth year is mentioned as 15.07.1997.
The alleged accident occurred on 04.12.2018 and hence it appears that as on the date of accident the age of the deceased is 22 years.
Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the age of the deceased is 22 years as on the date of accident.

Hence, in the absence of satisfactory evidence regarding avocation and income, this tribunal has relied upon notional income as per the chart issued by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Bengaluru and as per norms for the year 2018 the notional income is Rs.12,500/- p.m and hence, this tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.12,500/- p.m and it is multiplied by 12.

sentences.text: In the case on hand, undoubtedly the petitioner No.1 is the father, petitioner No.2 is the mother and petitioner No.3 is the sister of the deceased and they are the dependents on the earnings of the deceased.

In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017)
16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s (SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.3910/2019 Pranay Sethi & Others case, the future prospects or additional income should be added to monthly income of the deceased.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s (SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.3910/2019 Pranay Sethi & Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since deceased was aged below 40 years and was self employee at the time of accident, 40% income should be added to the monthly income towards future prospects which would be result in the income to be (12,500 + 5,000) = Rs.17,500/-.

It is also evident that the deceased in the present case was a bachelor and hence 50% of the income has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased and then his monthly income would be (17,500 - 8,750) = Rs.8,750/-.
The income of the deceased for the purpose of determining the loss of dependency would thus be Rs.8,750/-.
As the deceased was aged about 22 years, the multiplier of 18 would have to be applied.

Consequently the claimants would be entitled for a sum of Rs.18,90,000/-
(Rs.8,750 x 12 x 18) towards loss of dependency.

17. In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & Others case in respect to loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses, the aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of (SCCH-3) 15 M.V.C.No.3910/2019 10% in every 3 years.

sentences.text: Accordingly, in the head of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses, 10% is enhanced for period of every 3 years.
18. Medical Expenses:- The petitioners have got marked entire medical bills as per Ex.P.15, which amounts to Rs.18,16,438/-, Prescriptions as per Ex.P.14 and Advance bill receipts as per Ex.P.16.
In the cross-examination it is suggested that Sl. Nos.109 to 115 bill of Ex.P.14 there is no name of patient/deceased.
On perusal of said bills, there is no name of the deceased or his parents and hence, it is not accepted and hence, the total amount of said bills of Rs.30,120/- has to be deducted in total amount.
To disprove the said medical bills, the respondent No.1 has not produced any documents nor any evidence.
Therefore, after deducting the said amount, the petitioners are entitled for Rs.17,86,318/- under this head.
19. The claimant No.1 is the father, claimant No.2 is the mother and claimant No.3 is the sister of the deceased.
Therefore, petitioners No.1 and 2 would be entitled for Rs.48,400/- each towards loss of filial consortium.

In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported Sriram vs Suhalya Travels Pvt Ltd on 14 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113974092/
7 in Magma (SCCH-3) 16 M.V.C.No.3910/2019 General Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram alias Churu Ram reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130, the petitioner No.3 is entitled for Rs.40,000/- towards loss of love and affection and petitioners are entitled for Rs.19,500/- each towards loss of estate and funeral expenses and transportation of dead body.

sentences.text:
Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and noticing the number of dependents and 50% of the income taken into consideration towards the personal and living expenses of the deceased, this Tribunal has placed reliance on ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Pranay Sethi & others case has calculated compensation as under;
Sl.No. Head of Compensation Amount in Rs.
1. Loss of Dependency (After 18,90,000-00 deducting 50% of the income towards personal and living expenses)
2. Loss of filial consortium 96,800-00 (For petitioners No.1 and 2)
3. Loss of love and affection 40,000-00 (For petitioner No.3)
4. Loss of estate 19,500-00 (SCCH-3) 17 M.V.C.No.3910/2019 5.
Funeral expenses and 19,500-00 transportation of dead body
6. Medical expenses 17,86,318-00 Total 38,52,118-00 20.

Accordingly I hold that, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.38,52,118/-
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
21. Regarding liability:- On service of notice, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared, but respondent No.1 has not filed objections and not contested the matter.
The respondent No.2 has filed objections and contested the matter, but not lead any evidence to disprove the case of the petitioners and prove their contentions.
The petitioners have impleaded the respondents No.3 to 8 as Charge sheeted accused in these cases.

But their counsel argued that they are not the proper and necessary parties and in this regard they have produced copy of Oral Order of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in Writ Petition No.3830/2022 (GM-CPC) c/w Writ Petition No.3813/2022 (GM-CPC),
Writ Petition No.3818/2022 (SCCH-3) 18 M.V.C.No.3910/2019 (GM-CPC) and Writ Petition No.3822/2022 (GM-CPC), wherein it is held that the order of this court passed on 18.09.2021 is setaside and quashed.
Hence, on this order the claim petitions against respondents No.3 to 8 are dismissed.
The respondent No.2 in its written statement at para 7 admits issuance of insurance policy in respect of offending car and same is valid as on the date of accident.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the RC owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending car are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

However, since policy of offending vehicle was valid and is in force as on the date of accident, the respondent No.2 being the insurer of offending vehicle shall deposit above said compensation amount to the petitioners.
Accordingly, these Issues are answered partly in affirmative.

In view of reasons assigned to above Issues, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 are partly allowed with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.38,52,118/- (Rupees Thirty eight lakhs fifty two thousand one hundred and eighteen only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.1 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.
The claim petition against respondents No.3 to 8 is hereby dismissed.

The petitioner No.1 being the father, petitioner No.2 being the mother and petitioner No.3 being the sister of the deceased were apportioned the compensation in the ratio of 40-40-20, in the award amount together with interest.

The petitioners No.1 to 3 are entitled to get release 70% each of the award through E-payment directly to their account by obtaining the bank account details and remaining 30% each shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in their respective names.
The petitioners are at liberty to draw periodical interest.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The petitioners have filed this claim petition U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act, 1989, against the respondents for seeking compensation on account of death of one Sri.Ajith @ Ajith Kumar S/o Sriram, in the Motor Vehicle Accident.
The car in question did not involved in the accident nor caused accidental injuries to the petitioner and on the date of accident the car was being driven in a reasonable speed and careful manner and there was no rashness or negligence on the part of the driver of car and the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the omni car, in which deceased persons and petitioner were travelling.
The petition is bad for non-joinder of proper and necessary parties.
The compensation claimed is highly excessive, exaggerated and hence, pray for dismiss the petition with costs against respondent No.2.
05.
opennyai_summary.issue:
01. Whether petitioners prove that they are the LRs/dependents of deceased Sri.Ajith @ Ajith Kumar?
02. Whether petitioners prove that deceased Sri.Ajith @ Ajith Kumar was died in RTA arising out of the accident alleged to have been taken place on 04.12.2018 at about 11.50 p.m, near Kannamangala Palya Gate, BB Road, Devanahalli Taluk, Bengaluru District, due to negligent act of driver of Car bearing registration No.KA-03-NB-9119 as alleged in the petition?
03.
Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
04 . What order or award?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The PW.1/petitioner No.1 has stated that prior to accident deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 22 years and was doing private business as own work and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m. Due to untimely death of the deceased, the petitioners are put to great financial loss, loss of love and affection and mental agony.
14.
It is the duty of the petitioners to prove age of the deceased as on the date of accident.
The petitioners have not produced any birth certificate, school records or SSLC marks card of the deceased to show the exact date of birth of the deceased.
However, they have produced Ex.P.19 Aadhaar card of deceased.
Eventhough the said document is not authenticated document for the proof of age of any person, but in the absence of other evidence, said document can be relied upon and according to which his birth year is mentioned as 15.07.1997.
The alleged accident occurred on 04.12.2018 and hence it appears that as on the date of accident the age of the deceased is 22 years.
Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the age of the deceased is 22 years as on the date of accident.
Sriram vs Suhalya Travels Pvt Ltd on 14 August, 2025
As (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.3910/2019 per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and Ors. V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and Ors. case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 15 to 25 years is "18".
15. So far as avocation and income of deceased is concerned, the petitioners have not produced any evidence or documents regarding avocation and income of the deceased.
Since deceased was aged below 40 years and was self employee at the time of accident, 40% income should be added to the monthly income towards future prospects which would be result in the income to be (12,500 + 5,000) = Rs.17,500/-.
It is also evident that the deceased in the present case was a bachelor and hence 50% of the income has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased and then his monthly income would be (17,500 - 8,750) = Rs.8,750/-.
As the deceased was aged about 22 years, the multiplier of 18 would have to be applied.
17. In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & Others case in respect to loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses, the aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of (SCCH-3) 15 M.V.C.No.3910/2019 10% in every 3 years.
In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported Sriram vs Suhalya Travels Pvt Ltd on 14 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113974092/
7 in Magma (SCCH-3) 16 M.V.C.No.3910/2019 General Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram alias Churu Ram reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130, the petitioner No.3 is entitled for Rs.40,000/- towards loss of love and affection and petitioners are entitled for Rs.19,500/- each towards loss of estate and funeral expenses and transportation of dead body.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Consequently the claimants would be entitled for a sum of Rs.18,90,000/-
(Rs.8,750 x 12 x 18) towards loss of dependency.
Therefore, after deducting the said amount, the petitioners are entitled for Rs.17,86,318/- under this head.
Therefore, petitioners No.1 and 2 would be entitled for Rs.48,400/- each towards loss of filial consortium.
Funeral expenses and 19,500-00 transportation of dead body
Accordingly I hold that, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.38,52,118/-
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
Hence, on this order the claim petitions against respondents No.3 to 8 are dismissed.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the RC owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending car are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Accordingly, these Issues are answered partly in affirmative.
In view of reasons assigned to above Issues, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 are partly allowed with cost.
(SCCH-3) 19 M.V.C.No.3910/2019
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.38,52,118/- (Rupees Thirty eight lakhs fifty two thousand one hundred and eighteen only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.1 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.
The claim petition against respondents No.3 to 8 is hereby dismissed.
The petitioner No.1 being the father, petitioner No.2 being the mother and petitioner No.3 being the sister of the deceased were apportioned the compensation in the ratio of 40-40-20, in the award amount together with interest.
The petitioners No.1 to 3 are entitled to get release 70% each of the award through E-payment directly to their account by obtaining the bank account details and remaining 30% each shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in their respective names.
The petitioners are at liberty to draw periodical interest.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
